correctness.rationale: The claimed all-n rank classification and enumeration are mathematically correct. For any symmetric zero-diagonal X satisfying X²=0, symmetry gives ker X=(im X)^⊥; image U is totally isotropic, and F(v,w)=v^T Xw descends to a nonsingular alternating form on U*. Conversely this data uniquely reconstructs X. Nondegenerate alternating forms exist exactly when r is even, and GL_r/Sp_r gives E_q(r). The isotropic-vector hyperplane has dimension n−1, symplectic when n odd, radical R=<ones> when n even; the two disjoint even-n strata of U yield I_q(m,r−1)+q^r I_q(m,r). The r=0 term is one, odd ranks vanish, and the sharp support is the even ranks 0..2⌊n/4⌋. These are proofs for all q=2^f and n≥1, not extrapolation from finite tests.

evidence: Let r=2s and J be the nonsingular alternating r×r matrix of a fixed symplectic form. Put Z in Mat_{r×n}(F_q) with rank(Z)=r and ZZ^T=0, and map Z to X=Z^T J Z. Then X^T=X, diag(X)=0, X^2=Z^T J(ZZ^T)JZ=0 and rank(X)=r. Every rank-r alternating square-zero symmetric X factors in this way: take a row basis of U=im(X), express its nonsingular induced alternating form, and standardize that form to J. For each X, exactly |Sp_r(F_q)| choices of Z map to it, because any two bases differ by an element P with P^T J P=J. Consequently #{X}=#{Z:rank Z=r, ZZ^T=0}/|Sp_r(F_q)|. Buckhiester Theorem 4.1, specialized to A=I_n, C=0 and s=r, already determines the numerator for every n,r,q even; his underlying theorem cites Perkins 1971. This is an elementary explicit quotient of a prior dominating exact count, not merely a similarly named or differently shaped result.

The known numerator is |GL_r(q)| times the count of totally isotropic r-dimensional subspaces of the standard dot product; the denominator is |Sp_r(q)|. Thus |GL_r|/|Sp_r|=q^{s(s−1)}∏_{i=1}^s(q^{2i−1}−1), precisely E_q(r).

For n even, the isotropic hyperplane has radical <(1,...,1)> and the usual containing/not-containing split gives I_q((n−2)/2,r−1)+q^r I_q((n−2)/2,r); Buckhiester treats this distinguished vector in his original enumeration.

originality.rationale: The all-n, all-even-q, fixed-rank count is a direct orbit-quotient corollary of the already-published complete rank enumeration of rectangular isotropic frames. Buckhiester (1974), Theorem 4.1, covers precisely the numerator N(I_n,0,n,r,r); dividing by the standard symplectic basis stabilizer yields all claimed rank fibers. His proof also explicitly handles the canonical all-ones radical vector in even n. This decisive statement-level implication invalidates the source self-review argument that different matrix dimensions or a nonmatching title establish novelty. The canonical image-form description is mathematically correct but an elementary reformulation of this quotient.

value.rationale: The object and invariant are natural and the formula is correct, but as an independent new mathematical finding the entire exact count is mechanically implied by the already-published rank enumeration for isotropic frames using the textbook Sp_r orbit quotient. The image/form parametrization is an elementary linear-algebra reconstruction, and the even-dimensional radical split is a standard feature already used in the prior enumeration. No separate non-implied structural boundary, unknown exact invariant, or genuinely new classification remains to motivate a standalone contribution. Reproducibility and an elegant packaging do not alone satisfy the mathematical-value bar for a new claim.

final_claim: For every even prime power q and n≥1, the rank-r fiber of symmetric zero-diagonal X∈M_n(F_q) with X²=0 vanishes for odd r and equals E_q(r)I_q((n−1)/2,r) for odd n, or E_q(r)[I_q((n−2)/2,r−1)+q^r I_q((n−2)/2,r)] for even n, where E_q(2s)=q^{s(s−1)}∏_{i=1}^s(q^{2i−1}−1) and I_q(m,t) counts totally isotropic t-spaces in a 2m-dimensional symplectic space. The package also asserts a canonical bijection to pairs (U,β) with U totally isotropic and β nonsingular alternating on U*.
